# Phase One — Continuation Reconnaissance

The Awtsmoos renews the world before the next frame can appear;
Awtsmoos.com must therefore be judged by what is actually running here.
We do not repaint a fossil and call the living vessel whole;
we trace the route, the request, the scroll, the focus, the role.

## Mission boundary

Continue the existing Heichelos/post/social overhaul from the proven prior pass. Preserve working public selectors and behavior. Repair only from direct evidence. Close the completion gate through tests, browser behavior, console/network evidence, active CSS ownership, and final readback.

## Evidence already inherited

- The prior three planning files were read in full before this continuation.
- Auto-scroll now has a shared root resolver and document adapter.
- Reader controls, settings, action rail, discussion, and social core styles were already structurally rewritten.
- Production pace is intentionally around 45 WPM / contemplate / 15 px/s, so the old 120-WPM assumption is not authoritative.
- Community failure semantics intentionally distinguish transport failure from an empty discussion.
- The social application is scoped below `.awtsmoos-social-root` and must remain so.

## Work graph

1. Archaeology -> older Heichel/mobile/post notes -> architectural context.
2. Repository state -> git status/diff -> protect unrelated user work.
3. Auto-scroll production storage keys -> stale test contract -> rewrite whole test if proven stale.
4. Auto-scroll unit tests -> pass -> browser movement measurement.
5. Post template -> direct CSS roots -> recursive active import closure -> ownership/conflict scan.
6. Comments panel -> request builder -> `/comment-tree` -> server route -> runtime status/JSON/logs.
7. Post runtime -> Scribe's Lens -> menu/child views -> floating controls -> focus/reduced motion.
8. Heichel templates/bootstrap/styles -> route inventory -> mobile/tablet/desktop/RTL/LTR sweep.
9. Social bootstrap/imports/styles -> visible subsystem inventory -> mobile/desktop/accessibility sweep.
10. Entire Heichelos directory -> user-facing route inventory -> route-by-route completion checklist.
11. Touched files -> syntax/tests/wc/readback -> final delta and completion gate.

## Failure map

- A passing unit test can still hide a wrong browser scroll owner.
- A beautiful community card can still conceal a server contract failure.
- A clean touched-file grep can miss `!important` in a recursively imported active file.
- A mobile screenshot can miss focus traps, safe-area clipping, reduced-motion defects, or menu back-navigation failure.
- A social redesign can accidentally bleed into reader pages if root scoping is lost.
- Existing user edits can be destroyed if repository state is not read before writes.

## REMAINING_WORK

- Search and read older relevant Heichel/mobile/post archaeology.
- Inspect git status and relevant diffs.
- Read auto-scroll test and production storage/pacing/root modules in full.
- Prove the stale storage-key assumption, then rewrite the whole test only if evidence supports it.
- Run the two mandatory auto-scroll tests until both pass.
- Build the real active post CSS import closure and scan ownership/conflicts.
- Trace community transport client-to-server and verify it in the running app.
- Discover the real server command from package configuration.
- Browser-test post, Heichel, and social routes at required viewport classes.
- Fix every defect found with full-file rewrites and modular ownership.
- Re-run regressions after each repair family.
- Re-read every touched file and produce final verification/delta artifacts.

## NEXT_ACTION

Read older `.ai-thoughts` archaeology and repository state, then inspect the complete auto-scroll storage/test contract before any source rewrite.
